name: Sanitation & HACCP

objectives.text: Demonstrate the proper steps of handwashing before handling food
Describe basic sanitation practices used in a kitchen, such as cleaning surfaces and washing produce
Distinguish between cleaning and sanitizing a food contact surface
Identify sources of cross-contamination in a food preparation area
Explain how separating raw and ready-to-eat foods and using dedicated or color-coded tools prevents cross-contamination
Classify food safety hazards as biological, chemical, or physical and give an example of how each could enter a food product
Explain the purpose of critical control points in a food safety plan
Use a calibrated food thermometer to monitor and record cooking, cooling, and holding temperatures in a food lab
Sequence the seven principles of HACCP and describe what each principle accomplishes
Summarize the purposes of Sanitation Standard Operating Procedures and Good Manufacturing Practices in food processing facilities
Prepare a sanitizing solution and verify its concentration with test strips according to label directions
Apply HACCP principles to conduct a hazard analysis and identify critical control points in a food production process
Compare HACCP, Good Agricultural Practices, and Good Manufacturing Practices as systematic approaches to food safety from farm to processing plant
Outline procedures to control cross-contamination in a processing facility, including traffic flow, equipment sanitation, and allergen control
Apply Good Agricultural Practices for worker hygiene, water use, and harvest container sanitation in a produce SAE or school garden
Establish critical limits, monitoring procedures, and corrective actions for a critical control point
Evaluate temperature logs and sanitation records for compliance with a HACCP plan
Develop a Sanitation Standard Operating Procedure for cleaning and sanitizing a piece of food processing equipment
Analyze sanitation and temperature control practices used in food storage and distribution and recommend improvements
Design a HACCP plan for a specific food product, including hazard analysis, critical control points, monitoring, corrective actions, verification, and recordkeeping
Conduct a mock sanitation and HACCP verification audit of a school lab, meat processing facility, or SAE operation and report needed corrective actions
Evaluate a food recall or outbreak case to determine which sanitation practice or HACCP principle failed and how it could have been prevented

changes: Kept all six existing objectives, with light rewording to the grade 9 and grade 12 items to name hazard analysis and all HACCP plan elements. Added early hygiene and sanitation skills (handwashing, cleaning versus sanitizing, separating raw and ready-to-eat foods), hazard classification, and lab temperature monitoring. Added the seven HACCP principles plus high school competencies in SSOPs and GMPs, sanitizer verification, GAP for produce SAEs, critical limits and corrective actions, cross-contamination and allergen control, sanitation in storage and distribution, SSOP writing, mock audits, and recall case analysis. Microbiology of pathogens, labeling, and inspection grading were left to the sibling sub-topics. Standards were attached only at grades 9 to 12 where an objective directly teaches the standard.
